They Already Got The Money (Analysis)  (by Pablo Manríquez). ICE and CBP received $140 billion last year. They spent 11% of it. Senate Republicans want to give them more — and nobody can see where the rest went.

SCOOP: Home Depot Shareholders to Vote on Whether Parking Lot Cameras Are Helping ICE Find Customers (by Pablo Manríquez). A vote at the company's May 21 annual meeting could force the retail giant to account for how its license plate reader network may be enabling immigration enforcement near its stores.

They Said Discharge Petitions Don't Work on Immigration Policy. Ayanna Pressley Just Proved Them Wrong. (by Pablo Manríquez). Final vote on three-year extension of protections for 350,000 Haitians passed today 220-207.

"No Such Thing as Absolute Immunity" — ICE Agent Finally Faces Felony Charges (by Pablo Manríquez). A Hennepin County prosecutor just charged an ICE agent with felony assault. The Trump administration won't be happy. She doesn't care.
Five Immigration Stories That Should Be Leading the News (by Pablo Manríquez)

ICE Doesn't Need the Money. Republicans Want to Give It a Decade's Worth Anyway. (by Pablo Manríquez). Senate GOP is using a budget shortcut to fund an agency already financed through 2029 — and calling it an emergency.

Pope Leo Defies Trump White House (by Pablo Manríquez). My interview with Christopher Hale, creator of "Letters From Leo", on the first American Pope challenging Trump on war, artificial intelligence, and mass deportations.

An Unlikely Defender of Immigrant Crime Victims Inside the Trump Administration (by Pablo Manríquez). Trump's D.C. U.S. Attorney and former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro didn't just support U visa protections for crime victims "regardless of their legal status" — she demoted the staffer who refused to process them.

Canadian Firm With No ICE Experience Just Won $704 Million Arizona Warehouse Contract (by Pablo Manríquez). GardaWorld Federal Services is a new player in the U.S. migrant misery industry reshaping America's detention and deportation infrastructure.
Let's Meet at the Tune (by Pablo Manríquez)

Arrests Tripled. Warrants Didn't. Now DHS Is Being Sued. (by Pablo Manríquez). Eight Latino New Yorkers and a Syracuse workers' center say DHS agents are stopping and arresting people without warrants or probable cause — targeting brown skin, not criminal conduct.
Her Name Was Nilufar Easmin. (by Pablo Manríquez)

215,000 Demand Dilley Shutdown as Artists and Doctors Unite Against Family Detention (by Pablo Manríquez). Janelle Monáe, Spike Lee, Jodie Foster, and a battalion of pediatricians join growing coalition calling on CoreCivic and DHS to release children now

The Budget That Bets Against America’s Vulnerable (by Pablo Manríquez). A White House spending plan strips nearly $1.6 billion from programs serving migrant children and refugees — and that's just where the damage starts.
No Way In: How Trump Shut the Door on Iranian Refugees (by Pablo Manríquez). The last legal lifelines for Iranians fleeing persecution are gone. What remains is a gauntlet.
ACLU's Maribel Hernández Rivera:  La Constitución define Americano, no el presidente.

Jessica Craven discusses the importance of birthright citizenship outside the Supreme Court, emphasizing that individuals born in the United States belong here. She expresses her support for those who question their place, reinforcing the principles of the 14th amendment. This discussion provides a compelling perspective on constitutional law and us citizenship.
In case anyone here is interested in my art making. Otherwise I'll just post news. Nbd
Christian Maldonado joined ACLU outside of the Supreme Court on Wednesday where the Supreme Court heard oral arguments in the birthright citizenship case Barbara v Trump.
ACLU's Anthony Romero describe the vibe in the Supreme Court when Trump came to sit in on the birthright citizenship oral arguments on Wednesday.
